text:
Vancouver has not won in six games (0-6-0) and has been outscored 25-13 over that run. Our numbers say it's real: the Canucks have had only 43% of the expected goals, a measure of chance quality. The Rangers come in 4-1-0 after a 3-1 win in Calgary, playing without Alberts Smits and Sean Durzi. Marcus Pettersson also returns to Vancouver for the first time since leaving the Canucks, after 113 games with them.

The chance numbers favor New York. At five on five the Rangers have taken 53% of the expected goals, Vancouver 41%. Vancouver allows 3.74 expected goals per 60 minutes against New York's 2.89, and the Canucks take about four penalties a game, which keeps feeding power plays. In net, Dylan Garand (projected) is 1.7 goals saved above expected, meaning he has stopped more than his shots deserved. Leevi Meriläinen (projected) is at -2.1 this season and -17.9 last year. New York won the October meeting 6-2.

Watch Brock Boeser, one point from 500 and on a five-game point streak. With Filip Chytil out, he's up to 21:00 a night. For the Rangers, Mika Zibanejad is at 69% for a point, and J.T. Miller, a former Rangers pick facing his old organization's rival, is due after six games without a goal. Our under-the-radar picks: Oliver Bjorkstrand, a third-liner with 2.6 expected goals in his last 10 games, and Tye Kartye, at 51% for a point with more ice time and power-play work.
